title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: Paired estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (shared_initial_candidate) — A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study
abstract: Preregistered estimand and generation semantics (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37). We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1) comparing a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks using a deterministic validator. Under the frozen confirmatory semantics (shared_initial_candidate per pair) all confirmatory episodes completed and are archived: baseline = 120/120 verifier passes; guarded (gpt‑5‑mini, shared seed_0) = 120/120 verifier passes. Paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We (i) publish the exact execution and analysis artifacts and SHA‑256 fingerprints required for byte‑for‑byte reproduction, (ii) diagnose—using archived traces—why the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced a degenerate paired contingency (identical canonical candidates + deterministic validator), and (iii) provide runnable, artifact‑grounded experimental modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory design, validator diversity, and increased task heterogeneity) that preserve reproducibility while answering the operational question practitioners require: independent generative reliability.

sections.introduction: Translating operator intent into device configuration is a core NetOps task with safety‑critical correctness requirements: misordered or missing commands can break reachability, violate ACLs, or cause unsafe transient states during multi‑step changes. Deterministic, offline validators that compute forwarding/reachability and check ACL/routing policy invariants (Batfish‑class tools and successors) provide an operational oracle for pre‑deployment checks (see Batfish evolution [Brown et al., 2023; doi:10.1145/3603269.3604866]). Large language models (LLMs) can generate fluent device configurations from natural language intent, but their stochasticity and failure modes require careful, verifier‑grounded evaluation. Our preregistered paired study (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1) explicitly fixed the confirmatory estimand and generation semantics before observing model outputs: the estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663c...). This paper reports the archived execution, the preregistered statistical inference, an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of the degenerate paired outcome, and concrete, runnable recommendations for a reproducible rerun that answers independent generative reliability.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded evaluation and generate–validate–repair workflows are the dominant operational pattern for intent→configuration automation. Prior work differs on three methodologically consequential axes: (A) sampling semantics (single canonical candidate vs. independent per‑condition/multi‑seed sampling), (B) repair‑loop budget (single pass vs. bounded iterative repair), and (C) validator scope (syntactic parsing only vs. reachability/ACL/routing checks or multi‑verifier ensembles). Empirical studies emphasize that most repair gains occur early in bounded loops and that orchestration and feedback design often dominate raw model choice for repair effectiveness (see iterative‑repair literature in evidence bundle). Our study contributes a fully preregistered, artifact‑complete run and a transparent audit trail that shows how confirmatory design choices causally determine the estimand actually measured.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design. The study preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; SHA‑256 7db1663c...) specified: paired confirmatory design with N = 120 tasks (40 per topology class), primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate", one canonical generation per pair (seed_0), deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0), and analysis via paired_binary_analysis_v1 with 10,000 bootstrap resamples (bootstrap seed = 1729). All preregistered files and per‑artifact SHA‑256 fingerprints are published with the run (execution/execution_manifest.json). Task synthesis and templates. Tasks were programmatically generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and encode initial_state, expected_final_state, explicit required_sequence, and workflow_policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups). Representative task entries and canonical candidates are archived (e.g., execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8be..., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...). Model and orchestration. Declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini accessed via hosted_netops_gvr_v1; execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 a40e96e2...) documents exact runtime configuration. Deterministic validator and scoring. The validator enforces normalized parsing, transient safety checks and final_state assertions; the confirmatory scoring rule was full_intent_constraint_validation (binary pass/fail). Execution accounting and reproducibility. Planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; model_calls_used = 120 (single canonical generation per pair); failed_episode_count = 0. All provider call traces, call_cache artifacts, and per‑episode scoring traces are included to permit deterministic reruns.
sections.results: Confirmatory numerical results (artifact‑anchored). All confirmatory episodes completed and are archived. Aggregated counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 9c77c96f...) show baseline_success_count = 120/120 and guarded_success_count = 120/120 (complete_pair_count = 120). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...) is n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The preregistered primary estimator (mean of guarded_i − baseline_i over pairs) = 0.00. Bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Representative per‑episode validator traces (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...) record parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration and validation_after.valid = true for canonical candidates. Contamination heuristics were preregistered and run; their summary is archived at analysis/contamination_summary.csv (SHA‑256 389227f0...), but string‑overlap heuristics are imperfect proxies for pretraining exposure and cannot prove absence of related training data.
sections.discussion: Why the confirmatory contingency is degenerate: archived causal trace. The degenerate paired outcome directly follows from two preregistered, archived design choices: (1) generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (a single canonical LLM candidate per task archived at execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt; example SHA‑256 8f38c8be...) and (2) template‑tight tasks whose required_sequences and workflow_policies the canonical candidates satisfy. Because the deterministic validator maps identical inputs to identical outputs, identical canonical candidates produce identical pass/fail outcomes across both conditions, collapsing the paired contingency to n_11 = 120. This causal chain is visible in the archived provider traces, shared initial candidate files, and scoring JSONs and permits exact audit and reproduction (see execution/execution_manifest.json). Operational interpretation and recommended runnable reruns. The confirmatory test correctly answers its preregistered estimand (verifier‑consistency under identical inputs) but does not estimate independent generative reliability (the practical probability that independently drawn LLM outputs pass the verifier). Using the published artifacts one can deterministically execute informative reruns that answer the operational question: (A) independent_per_condition rerun — generate distinct seeds per condition per task (baseline seed_0, guarded seed_1), rescore with the same deterministic validator and compute paired contrasts; (B) multi‑seed confirmatory design — draw K ≥ 3 independent seeds per condition per task and estimate per‑condition pass probabilities with bootstrap CIs; (C) validator diversification — run a second independent verifier and report intersection/union pass rates. Because every element (task generator, model configuration, provider calls, and validator) is archived with SHA‑256 fingerprints, these reruns are deterministic and auditable.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired experiment and released a complete artifact bundle enabling byte‑level reproduction (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics both the deterministic template baseline and the gpt‑5‑mini guarded condition validated on all N = 120 tasks (both 120/120). Archived artifacts demonstrate that identical canonical candidates per pair and template‑tight task constraints caused the degenerate paired outcome; consequently the confirmatory paired result does not provide evidence about independent LLM generative reliability in operational settings. We provide artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory execution, validator diversification, task heterogeneity expansion) that preserve reproducibility and enable informative independent comparisons. All execution and analysis artifacts—including the immutable master prompt reference (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and the preregistration SHA‑256—are included in the submission bundle to permit exact audit and follow‑up experiments. Transparent preregistration combined with exhaustive artifact publication clarifies precisely what a confirmatory test measures and accelerates corrective reruns that answer NetOps practitioners' operational questions.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
